writeup.headline: Charles River rates Hold: a strong balance sheet and price trend offset falling revenue and rich valuation.
writeup.thesis: CRL scores 53, a Hold, because its strongest factors pull in opposite directions from its weakest. The balance sheet scores 100 with net cash (net debt to FCF of -0.5), and the trend scores 100, with the price at its 52-week high, 69.8% above its 200-day average and shares 119.2 pp ahead of SPY over the last 126 trading days. Growth is weak at 23, with a latest-quarter revenue decline of 2.7% year on year, a TTM revenue decline of 0.7%, and growth slowed by 3.9 pp from the previous quarter. Valuation scores just 15: in absolute terms the multiples are high (P/S of 4.5x, P/FCF of 48.2x, EV/EBIT of 196.0x, FCF yield 2.9 pp below the 10-year Treasury yield), and the stock is expensive against its own history, with P/FCF more expensive than at 60 of the last 61 month-ends. Quality is middling at 60, with an operating margin of 2.2% but an FCF margin of 9.3% and diluted share count down 2.6% year on year.
key_risks: Revenue is shrinking and growth slowed by 3.9 pp, which is at odds with a share price at its 52-week high.
Valuation is high in absolute terms (EV/EBIT of 196.0x) and expensive against its own history, leaving little room for disappointment.
After a sharp run (price 25.1% above its 50-day average), any pullback could be steep.
A thin 2.2% operating margin means small revenue misses can hit earnings hard.
Q3 results on Nov 4 could fail to back up the raised guidance and the Investor Day targets.
what_would_change: Up to Buy (12 points away): growth would need to turn back to positive revenue growth, or the valuation would need to ease after a price pullback or stronger earnings.
Down to Sell (9 points below): a fade in the trend score from its current 100, or a weak Q3 report that cuts guidance and hurts growth and news scores, could push it below 45.
Improving operating margin from 2.2% would lift quality and make the EV/EBIT multiple look less extreme.
